read "/Users/user/Obsidian/hex-rays/hcli/Proposal IDAPython Environment Consistency.md"

Now, I'd like to develop a specific plan of action for the implementation Of the changes to HCLI to support this proposal. There are three things we need to do. First In the appropriate places, we need to recognize when someone's Python environment is not configured according to the best practices. Of course, there should be a command line flag in appropriate places that allows the user to bypass this warning to silence it. But most users should see this by the default if they've done something unexpected. Second, we need a command like hcli pyth ida python doctor To triage the environment and propose specific fixes to the user's environment. Tell them what violates the best practices and what they should do about it. Third, we need to build the tool to create an environment for the user that adheres to the best practices So this would be something like HCLI. python create environment. And that's described in the document. So these are the three phases there. I want you to look at what we currently have in HCLI, identify all of the places where we need to make changes, and what you'd propose to do in order to affect these three goals. Take your time, be thorough comprehensive, and what I'd really love is to drastically improve the quality of the messages in terms of what we show to users, telling them what is wrong, what is recommended, and how they can get there. And taking into account as many possible setups, such as those enumerated in the document, such that we can take into account those possible setups, recognize them, and tell them what they need to improve. Go ahead. As you come up with a final plan, I want you to write it into the same directory as the proposal. It should be a planning document in that same obsidian directory and we'll collaborate on it to come up with a Thorough plan of action
I'll start by reading the proposal document and then exploring the current HCLI codebase to understand what exists today.

1	[Willi Ballenthin](mailto:wballenthin@hex-rays.com) on Sep 10, 2026
2	https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit?usp=sharing
3	
4	| Status: Drafting as of Sep 10, 2026\. Please add comments and/or edit directly (in “Suggesting” mode ![][image1]). The more feedback the better. [Willi Ballenthin](mailto:wballenthin@hex-rays.com) believes that sharing the final draft is only 50% of the impact; the journey of crafting the draft together is at least as important. Timeline: Sep 10, 2026 initial draft, shared with [Pierre-Alexandre Losson](mailto:palosson@hex-rays.com) and [Duncan Ogilvie](mailto:dogilvie@hex-rays.com) Future: shared with all@hex-rays.com |
5	| :---- |
6	
7	| TL;DR:  We will strongly recommend the following setup for using Python with IDA: require a virtual environment, do not use global Python environments use `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` to specify the venv the venv interpreter version must match whats registered with `idapyswitch` And we will do this by: HCLI will audit and warn or reject environments, at least when installing plugins but, HCLI can create and configure the recommended setup updating our public documentation docs.hex-rays.com Historically, Hex-Rays has been very lenient in accepting many Python configurations. Now we're hitting a lot of problems in the plugin ecosystem. So we propose to encourage a more  consistent environment to reduce compatibility issues. |
8	| :---- |
9	
10	## The problem
11	
12	IDA allows users to link almost any Python interpreter via `idapyswitch`. It can be a system Python, a Homebrew Python, a Windows Store Python, a framework Python, or one inside a virtual environment. IDA stores the choice as a path to a `libpython` shared library in a registry, and at runtime it loads that library and initializes the embedded interpreter.
13	
14	HCLI needs to install Python packages (plugin dependencies) into whatever environment IDA is using. To do that, HCLI must answer two questions: *which Python executable does IDA use?* and *can we pip-install into it?* This is hard, and the combinatorial complexity of IDA's Python configurability results in many HCLI support requests. With Assist and the Malware Analysis addon likely to use HCLI/plugin manager for distribution, we need a clear set of recommendations and fixes.
15	
16	## Recommended setup
17	
18	The proposed opinionated setup requires four things:
19	
20	1. Users must use a virtual environment, which eliminates PEP 668 externally-managed errors, permission problems with system Pythons, and conflicts with OS-managed packages. The recommended location is `~/.idapro/venv`.  
21	2. The venv should be created with pip available (`uv venv --seed`).  
22	3. Users should set `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` to point at the venv's Python interpreter. This is not strictly required but recommended.  
23	4. The venv interpreter version must match what `idapyswitch` registered (e.g., if `idapyswitch` registered `libpython3.12`, the venv must use Python 3.12).
24	
25	If these four conditions hold, HCLI's entire `_derive_python_exe` heuristic becomes unnecessary. This is good, because it is currently very complicated and error prone. The resolution path collapses to: read `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE`, verify the executable exists and its version matches, install packages. We can avoid probing how idat behaves and avoid platform-specific special cases, which is good. Incidentally, it also enables the plugin manager to work with IDA Home and IDA Free, since those don't ship with idat.
26	
27	`IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` is an environment variable that IDA already supports \- it's not being proposed or implemented here. We just need to get people to use it reliably.
28	
29	At the very least, users must use a virtual environment and get IDA to recognize it through some means, such as by modifying [`idapythonrc.py`](http://idapythonrc.py).
30	
31	## How we get there
32	
33	Step 0: sufficient agreement and commitment to this document. Key stakeholders include [Andrey Dybov](mailto:adybov@hex-rays.com) and the API/SDK team, [Julian Kirsch](mailto:jkirsch@hex-rays.com) for their familiarity and knack for Linux, [Igor Skochinsky](mailto:igor@hex-rays.com) due to contextual knowledge and customer-facing role, and [Pierre-Alexandre Losson](mailto:palosson@hex-rays.com) for cross-product integration.
34	
35	First, we will update our online documentation with clear instructions on how to configure their system to use IDA with a Python virtual environment. [Willi Ballenthin](mailto:wballenthin@hex-rays.com) has an [agent skill](https://github.com/williballenthin/idawilli/blob/master/.claude/skills/ida-and-github-actions/SKILL.md) that can be migrated into the Hex-Rays marketplace that explains how to use IDA and Python in GitHub Actions/Docker/CI/CD.
36	
37	HCLI will detect and warn (or bail) when it encounters a non-recommended setup, at least when interacting with the plugin manager `hcli plugin …`. If it cannot recognize `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE`, and possibly not recognize a virtual environment when falling back to `idat` probing, then it will tell the user to fix their setup. HCLI can give environment-specific feedback, like “run this command xxxx to create a venv on your system using the already available Python 3.13.15”. HCLI can also link to the clear documentation on [docs.hex-rays.com](http://docs.hex-rays.com).
38	
39	HCLI can create recommended environments for users, such as with a new subcommand like `hcli ida python create-environment`. This would create a new seeded virtual environment at `$IDAUSR/venv/` and configure `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` using platform appropriate mechanisms (or give the user an option to do this themselves). With this in place, provisioning a new system with IDA becomes:
40	
41	```shell
42	hcli ida install ...
43	hcli ida python create-environment
44	```
45	
46	Or possibly even:
47	
48	```shell
49	hcli ida install --create-python-environment ...
50	```
51	
52	## Non-recommended setups
53	
54	Users arrive at many different Python configurations depending on their OS, how they installed IDA, and what advice they found online. Here are some of them:
55	
56	The most common setup is no setup at all: install IDA, do nothing about Python. On Linux and macOS, IDA uses whatever system Python `idapyswitch` finds. On Windows, the installer can bundle a private Python via `--install_python`. In both cases the Python environment is not writable by HCLI for package installation. On Ubuntu 24.04+ and Debian, pip refuses to install anything because the system Python is marked externally-managed (PEP 668). On Windows, `sys.executable` inside IDA reports `idat.exe` rather than the Python interpreter, and PATH-based fallback can find the Windows Store shim instead of the real Python. This default-by-inaction configuration is the source of many support requests.
57	
58	Power users (especially on macOS) install Python through Homebrew, pyenv, or Anaconda, then run `idapyswitch` to register that Python's `libpython` with IDA. Without a venv, package installation still affects the global environment. Homebrew Python on macOS may also be PEP 668 externally-managed. Anaconda environments are not standard venvs (no `pyvenv.cfg`), so HCLI's venv detection does not recognize them. pyenv shims can confuse PATH-based fallback. macOS framework Pythons report misleading `sys.base_prefix` values, causing HCLI to misidentify the interpreter.
59	
60	Some users create a venv, activate it in their shell, and launch IDA from that terminal. IDA 9.0+ picks up modules from the activated venv, and the 9.0 release notes describe this approach in a single sentence. It only works when IDA is launched from an activated terminal session. Desktop shortcuts, file associations, and system launchers don't carry the shell activation, so IDA reverts to the base Python. When HCLI is invoked from a different terminal, it won't see `$VIRTUAL_ENV` either.
61	
62	There's also a community-recommended approach to add venv activation code to `~/.idapro/idapythonrc.py`. A [Hex-Rays community post](https://community.hex-rays.com/t/using-a-virtualenv-for-idapython/261) describes the technique: use `site.addsitedir()` to inject the venv's `site-packages` into `sys.path` at IDA startup. This works for interactive IDA, but HCLI's batch-mode probe (`idat -A -S<script>`) does not execute `idapythonrc.py` the same way. The probe sees the base system Python while interactive IDA uses the venv. Users confirm their setup works inside IDA, yet HCLI installs packages into the wrong location. Since `idapythonrc.py` is arbitrary Python code, its hard to inspect and decide how it affect the Python environment. I (Willi) am responsible for the community.hex-rays.com post, and I've subsequently come to realize that `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` is a much better solution.
63	
64	Users familiar with `uv` sometimes create a venv with `uv venv ~/.idapro/venv` but omit the `--seed` flag. The resulting venv has no pip installed. HCLI finds the correct Python but fails with `PipNotAvailableError` when it tries to install plugin dependencies. The fix (`uv venv --seed`) is not obvious from the error message. A related problem: users who run `uv run --with ida-hcli hcli <command>` instead of installing HCLI globally cause `uv` to create an ephemeral cache environment and set `$VIRTUAL_ENV` to point at it, hiding the user's actual IDA venv. If HCLI's overlay detection fails, it installs into the ephemeral environment, which is discarded after the command exits. While this is a bug in HCLI, its been really tricky to find and maintain.
65	
66	Finally, on systems where Python is not installed or `idapyswitch` was never run, IDA starts without IDAPython. IDA 9.4 does not crash in this case, but HCLI's probe fails entirely and no plugin operations are possible.
67	
68	The recommended setup (`IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` pointing at a properly versioned venv with pip) avoids these failure modes. It provides a single, verifiable state that HCLI can check without spawning IDA.
69	
70	## Additional Background Information
71	
72	### Current state of IDA documentation
73	
74	The official documentation at [docs.hex-rays.com](https://docs.hex-rays.com/) provides almost no guidance on Python configuration. A user who reads the relevant pages learns very little about how to set up Python for IDA. Here's what we (Willi and his agents) found on 2026-09-09 against IDA 9.4-era docs.
75	
76	The [installation page](https://docs.hex-rays.com/getting-started/install-ida.md) says "Make sure Python 3 or later is installed on your computer for the IDAPython API to function properly" and nothing else about Python. This sentence is identical across macOS, Linux, and Windows sections. It does not say which Python, how to verify it, or what happens with multiple Python installations. The [installer command-line options](https://docs.hex-rays.com/getting-started/install-ida/ida-installer-commandline-options.md) page documents a Windows-only `--install_python` flag to bundle Python 3, and notes "On Linux and Mac, the system-wide Python is presumed to be available."
77	
78	The [IDAPython landing page](https://docs.hex-rays.com/developer/idapython.md), [getting started guide](https://docs.hex-rays.com/developer/idapython/idapython-getting-started.md), and [how-tos](https://docs.hex-rays.com/developer/idapython/how-tos.md) cover the API (modules, constants, code snippets, plugin structure) but contain no information about interpreter selection, virtual environments, pip, or environment setup.
79	
80	The [plugin publishing guide](https://docs.hex-rays.com/developer/publishing-plugins/how-tos/plugin-publishing.md) documents the `pythonDependencies` field in `ida-plugin.json` and states that "HCLI automatically places plugins in the correct locations, installs required Python dependencies, and handles additional setup tasks." There is no guidance for what to do when that automatic installation fails (PEP 668, missing pip, wrong Python).
81	
82	The [environment variables page](https://docs.hex-rays.com/core/disassembler/concepts/environment-variables.md) lists \~35 IDA environment variables, none Python-related. `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE`, `PYTHONPATH`, `VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `IDAPYSWITCH` are all absent. The [configuration files page](https://docs.hex-rays.com/core/user-interface/concepts/configuration-files.md) lists `IDAPYTHON.CFG` as a config file without explaining its contents, location, or usage. The [troubleshooting pages](https://docs.hex-rays.com/core/user-interface/troubleshooting.md) cover disassembly/analysis issues only, with no Python entries.
83	
84	The [idalib getting started guide](https://docs.hex-rays.com/core/idalib/getting-started.md) shows `uv pip install idapro` and running `py-activate-idalib.py`, the closest the docs come to showing Python environment management. But this is specific to idalib and does not cover the IDA desktop application.
85	
86	Release notes contain more Python environment information than the documentation itself. The [IDA 9.0 release notes](https://docs.hex-rays.com/release-notes/9_0.md) announce venv support in one sentence: "simply run IDA from an activated virtual environment and it will pick up locally installed modules." This is the only mention of venv support in the entire documentation. No setup steps, no explanation of what "activated" means here, no mention of `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE`. The same release notes note that `idapyswitch` can now work "with read-only IDA installations" and "detect recent homebrew versions on macOS." The [IDA 9.4 release notes](https://docs.hex-rays.com/release-notes/9_4.md) add one-line changelog entries for "detect/support pythons managed by uv/anaconda/homebrew," "warn on libpython/venv version mismatch," and "don't crash on launch when Python is not configured," without explaining what users should do about any of them.
87	
88	The following topics have no documentation at all: `idapyswitch` (appears only in changelogs), `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE`, `idapythonrc.py` (users find it via [community forums](https://community.hex-rays.com/t/using-a-virtualenv-for-idapython/261) or sample files), virtual environment setup for IDA (creation, location, version matching), the requirement that the venv Python version match the `libpython` registered with `idapyswitch`, pip/package installation into IDA's environment, and Python-specific troubleshooting (PEP 668, wrong interpreter detection, common error messages).
89	
90	### Collection of Challenges
91	
92	#### Challenge: Finding the right Python executable
93	
94	IDA does not expose which Python interpreter it uses via any config file or queryable API. The `idapyswitch` registry stores a path to `libpython3.X.so` (or `.dylib`/`.dll`), but that library path does not directly tell you the corresponding `python3` executable. For example, when the user wants to use a virtual environment, the `libpython` path might be far removed on the file system. HCLI's only reliable method is to spawn IDA in batch mode (`idat -A -S<script>`) and run a probe script that prints `sys.prefix`, `sys.base_prefix`, `sys.executable`, and related values. Then HCLI runs an 85-line heuristic (`_derive_python_exe`) to work backwards from those values to an actual executable path.
95	
96	We could parse the IDA registry for this data, but we've avoid this today so that we don't duplicate code and possibly bugs.
97	
98	Anyways, this probe-and-derive approach is fragile because each platform and Python distribution reports different values.
99	
100	On Windows, `sys.executable` returns the path to `idat.exe` rather than the Python interpreter ([\#133](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/133)). On macOS with IDA 9.4+, `sys.executable` is also the idat binary. Therefore, HCLI cannot trust this value and must derive the executable from `sys.prefix` using platform-specific path layouts. When `sys.executable` fails and HCLI falls back to searching PATH, but we found that it would find the Windows Store `python3.EXE` shim instead of the Python configured via `idapyswitch` ([\#154](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/154)). HCLI now detects and rejects these shims.
101	
102	When HCLI itself runs inside a virtual environment (during CI or development), environment variables like `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `PYTHONHOME`, and `PYTHONPATH` leak into the `idat` subprocess, causing IDA to bind to the wrong interpreter ([\#178](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/178)). HCLI now scrubs these variables before launching idat. On macOS, framework Pythons can report the base framework prefix even when running inside a venv, requiring additional validation against known venv roots.
103	
104	Beyond correctness, the probe is slow. Spawning IDA as a subprocess can take a second or so ([\#288](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/288)). For one-off plugin installs this is tolerable, but if a hypothetical MCP server called `hcli ida python run-script` on every invocation then a multi-second startup penalty is not acceptable. Caching the probe results is risky because IDA stores Python configuration in many places and a stale cache would produce hard-to-debug failures.
105	
106	The entire probe mechanism also depends on `idat`, the text-mode IDA executable. IDA Home and IDA Free editions don't ship `idat`, so plugin installation fails immediately with `Error: can't find idat` ([\#196](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/196), [\#22](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/22)).
107	
108	#### Challenge: Installing packages into IDA's environment
109	
110	Even after finding the right Python, HCLI often cannot install packages into it.
111	
112	Modern Linux distributions (Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian) and some macOS installations mark their system Python with PEP 668's `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` marker. When IDA uses this system Python (the default on a fresh install), pip refuses to install anything ([\#275](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/275), [\#144](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/144)). Users see `error: externally-managed-environment` and have no idea what to do. Some of them attempt to remove the marker file using admin privileges, but this just delays confusion. Even without PEP 668, some system Python environments live in locations the user cannot write to (`/usr/lib/python3/...`), so `pip install` fails with permission errors.
113	
114	A separate problem: users who create virtual environments with `uv venv` (without `--seed`) get an environment that has no pip installed ([\#124](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/124)). HCLI detects the correct Python but then fails with `PipNotAvailableError`.
115	
116	#### Challenge: Virtual environment detection gaps
117	
118	Virtual environments solve the package installation problem, but HCLI has historically struggled to detect them.
119	
120	A common setup is to activate a venv in `idapythonrc.py`, which runs at IDA startup ([source](https://community.hex-rays.com/t/using-a-virtualenv-for-idapython/261)). But HCLI's batch-mode probe (`idat -A -S<script>`) does not trigger `idapythonrc.py` the same way as interactive IDA (setting `IDA_IS_INTERACTIVE`). The probe sees the base system Python while IDA interactively uses the venv ([\#144](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/144)). Users confirm their venv works in IDA, yet HCLI installs packages into the wrong location.
121	
122	Until [\#279](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/279), HCLI did not check `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` at all, so users who configured their venv via this variable still had HCLI probe idat and find a different Python. Even after that fix, version mismatches go undetected in normal operation: a user can register Python 3.12 with `idapyswitch` but point `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` at a Python 3.14 venv. IDA loads `libpython3.12` at startup but the venv's packages are installed for 3.14, producing confusing import failures. HCLI warns about this in `explain-environment` ([\#278](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/278)), but not during normal plugin operations.
123	
124	A subtler problem: when HCLI is invoked via `uv run --with ida-hcli`, uv creates an ephemeral cache environment and sets `$VIRTUAL_ENV` to point at it, hiding the user's actual venv. HCLI uses three independent heuristics to detect these overlays (path under uv cache dirs, uv-internal ancestor directories, `extends-environment` key in `pyvenv.cfg`).
125	
126	#### Aside: The codebase cost
127	
128	The complexity of IDA's Python configurability shows up directly in HCLI's codebase. `python.py` (\~940 lines) contains the core resolution logic: an 85-line `_derive_python_exe` heuristic with special cases for Windows Store shims, macOS framework Pythons, IDA 9.4+ macOS, and PEP 668 environments, plus a three-level precedence chain in `resolve_current_python` (`$HCLI_CURRENT_IDA_PYTHON_EXE` \> `$IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` \> idat probe). `venv.py` (\~300 lines) handles virtual environment detection, uv cache discrimination, and version probing. `explain_environment.py` (\~700 lines) is a diagnostic command that exists solely because the environment has so many interacting pieces: it probes IDA, checks venvs, validates version consistency, detects PEP 668, warns about uv overlays, and surfaces misconfigurations.
129	
130	Nearly 2000 lines of code exist to answer the question "which Python does IDA use and can we install packages there?"
131	
132	## Open questions
133	
134	A program that uses idalib (IDA as a library) typically has its own virtual environment with its own dependencies. That venv's `site-packages` may not include IDA plugin dependencies, which live in the potentially-separate dedicated IDA virtualenv. How should idalib programs access plugin packages? Options include adding the IDA venv's site-packages to `sys.path`, requiring idalib programs to install plugin deps into their own venv, or having HCLI provide a path helper.
135	
136	Should HCLI refuse to operate without a venv, or only warn? Refusing would break existing users who have working non-venv setups. Warning is less disruptive but doesn't prevent the support requests.
137	
138	The setup requires users to create a venv manually. Should HCLI or the IDA installer create one automatically? Auto-creation reduces friction but risks choosing the wrong Python version, location, or permissions.
139	
140	Even with a shared venv, plugins can have conflicting dependencies. A full solution might require per-plugin virtual environments or a dependency resolver, both much more complex than the current approach. Perhaps this could be addressed in IDA core sometime beyond IDA 9.5.
141	
142	## Related issues
143	
144	Issues from the [HCLI tracker](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues) related to this problem space. See the descriptions above for how each fits into the overall picture.
145	
146	[\#288](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/288), [\#178](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/178), [\#154](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/154), [\#133](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/133), [\#277](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/277) (Python executable detection); [\#279](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/279), [\#278](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/278), [\#275](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/275), [\#144](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/144) (virtual environments); [\#291](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/291), [\#265](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/265), [\#124](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/124), [\#34](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/34), [\#171](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/171), [\#58](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/58) (dependency/package installation); [\#272](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/272), [\#153](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/153) (Python version compatibility); [\#314](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/314), [\#292](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/292), [\#196](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/196), [\#155](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/155), [\#108](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/108), [\#85](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/85), [\#25](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/25), [\#23](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/23), [\#22](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-hcli/issues/22) (installation/configuration).  
147

453	@dataclass(frozen=True)
454	class PythonVersionMismatch:
455	    """A Python environment whose version disagrees with IDA's embedded Python.
456	
457	    idapyswitch records which libpython IDA loads, and that library alone
458	    determines `sys.version_info` inside IDA.  Activating a virtualenv (via
459	    idapythonrc.py) doesn't change it: a venv only redirects `sys.path`.  So a
460	    venv built for a different major.minor version cannot supply working
461	    packages to IDA -- extension modules are ABI-incompatible, and even pure
462	    Python packages land in a `site-packages` directory that IDA's interpreter
463	    never looks at.  This is essentially always a misconfiguration.
464	    """
465	
466	    # major.minor of IDA's embedded Python, as registered by idapyswitch
467	    ida_version: str
468	    # major.minor of the mismatched environment
469	    other_version: str
470	    # the mismatched environment: a virtualenv root or a Python executable
471	    other_path: Path
472	    # human-readable description of where `other_path` came from
473	    other_source: str
474	
475	
476	def find_python_version_mismatches(info: IdatProbe, python_exe: Path | None) -> list[PythonVersionMismatch]:
477	    """Find Python environments whose version disagrees with IDA's embedded Python.
478	
479	    `info` is the result of running GET_PYTHON_INFO_PY inside IDA, which reports
480	    both `sys.version_info` and the virtualenv IDA activated for itself.
481	
482	    `python_exe` is the interpreter hcli would use to install plugin
483	    dependencies, or None when it couldn't be detected, in which case only the
484	    virtualenvs described by `info` are checked.
485	
486	    Environments that can't be inspected are skipped, so this is best-effort:
487	    an empty result doesn't prove the environment is consistent.
488	    """
489	    ida_version = f"{info.version_major}.{info.version_minor}"
490	    mismatches: list[PythonVersionMismatch] = []
491	
492	    # venv roots already reported, so a venv reached two different ways
493	    # (its $VIRTUAL_ENV and its interpreter) is only reported once
494	    seen_venvs: set[str] = set()
495	
496	    candidate_venvs = [
497	        (info.virtual_env, "the virtualenv activated inside IDA ($VIRTUAL_ENV)"),
498	        (
499	            _get_venv_root_from_python(info.idapython_venv_executable),
500	            "the virtualenv requested by $IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE",
501	        ),
502	    ]
503	
504	    for venv, source in candidate_venvs:
505	        if not venv:
506	            continue
507	
508	        normalized = _normalize_path(str(venv))
509	        if normalized is None or normalized in seen_venvs:
510	            continue
511	        seen_venvs.add(normalized)
512	
513	        version = get_virtual_env_version(venv)
514	        if version is not None and version != ida_version:
515	            mismatches.append(
516	                PythonVersionMismatch(
517	                    ida_version=ida_version,
518	                    other_version=version,
519	                    other_path=Path(venv),
520	                    other_source=source,
521	                )
522	            )
523	
524	    # The interpreter hcli installs plugin dependencies with. When it's a venv
525	    # python, this usually restates a mismatch found above; when detection fell
526	    # back to a base interpreter, it can differ from IDA's Python on its own.
527	    if python_exe is None:
528	        return mismatches
529	
530	    exe_venv = _get_venv_root_from_python(str(python_exe))
531	    if exe_venv is None or _normalize_path(str(exe_venv)) not in seen_venvs:
532	        version = probe_python_version(python_exe)
533	        if version is not None and version != ida_version:
534	            mismatches.append(
535	                PythonVersionMismatch(
536	                    ida_version=ida_version,
537	                    other_version=version,
538	                    other_path=python_exe,
539	                    other_source="the interpreter hcli would install plugin dependencies into",
540	                )
541	            )
542	
543	    return mismatches
544

546	def format_python_version_mismatch_warning(mismatches: list[PythonVersionMismatch]) -> str:
547	    """Render mismatches as a rich-markup warning, or "" when there are none."""
548	    if not mismatches:
549	        return ""
550	
551	    ida_version = mismatches[0].ida_version
552	    lines = [
553	        "[bold yellow]Warning:[/bold yellow] IDA's Python version does not match the active virtualenv.",
554	        f"  IDA's embedded Python is {ida_version}, which is what idapyswitch registered.",

609	class ScriptNotFoundError(RuntimeError):

613	# Script run by IDA's Python interpreter (not by idat).
614	# Locates the wrapper executable installed for a console script, like `speakeasy`.
615	#
616	# There is no API for this. Package metadata declares the entry point
617	# (`speakeasy = speakeasy.__main__:main`), which is a Python object reference, not a
618	# file: the wrapper is generated at install time and where it lands is up to the
619	# installer. see: https://discuss.python.org/t/can-i-retrieve-the-path-for-an-entry-point-using-importlib-metadata/79490
620	#
621	# So we resolve it in two steps:
622	#
623	#  1. the distribution's RECORD, via `Distribution.files`. This is the installer's own
624	#     list of the files it wrote, including generated scripts, which appear as paths
625	#     relative to site-packages, like `../../../bin/speakeasy`. It's authoritative:
626	#     the wrapper it names belongs to the same environment as the package we matched.
627	#     pip and uv both write RECORD, as does any wheel-spec-compliant installer.
628	#     (Debian strips it from apt-packaged distributions, but those interpreters are
629	#     externally managed, so we don't support installing into them anyway.)
630	#
631	#  2. otherwise, look for the file in the scripts directories, which is where the
632	#     wheel spec says installers should put it. This is only name matching, so it can
633	#     turn up a stale or unrelated script - hence it comes second.
634	#
635	# The wrapper's filename matches the entry point name by convention, not by rule.
636	# Windows installers generate a `name.exe` trampoline; older setuptools also left a
637	# `name-script.py` beside it.
638	GET_SCRIPT_INFO_PY = r"""
639	import io
640	import json
641	import os
642	import sys
643	import sysconfig
644	
645	# ensure UTF-8 output for unicode install paths
646	if hasattr(sys.stdout, "buffer"):
647	    sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, encoding="utf-8")
648	
649	name = sys.argv[1]
650	
651	if os.name == "nt":
652	    filenames = [name + ".exe", name + ".cmd", name + ".bat", name, name + "-script.py"]
653	else:
654	    filenames = [name]
655	
656	# Scan distributions for the entry point, rather than using entry_points(name=...)
657	# or EntryPoint.dist, which need Python 3.10+. IDA may be using an older interpreter.
658	entry_point = None
659	record_candidates = []
660	try:
661	    from importlib.metadata import distributions
662	
663	    for dist in distributions():
664	        try:
665	            eps = [
666	                ep
667	                for ep in dist.entry_points
668	                if ep.name == name and ep.group in ("console_scripts", "gui_scripts")
669	            ]
670	        except Exception:
671	            continue
672	
673	        if not eps:
674	            continue
675	
676	        entry_point = {
677	            "name": eps[0].name,
678	            "value": eps[0].value,
679	            "group": eps[0].group,
680	            "distribution": dist.metadata["Name"],
681	            "version": dist.version,
682	        }
683	
684	        # `files` is None when the distribution has no RECORD
685	        for file in dist.files or []:
686	            if os.path.basename(str(file)) not in filenames:
687	                continue
688	            try:
689	                record_candidates.append(os.path.realpath(str(dist.locate_file(file))))
690	            except Exception:
691	                pass
692	
693	        break
694	except Exception:
695	    pass
696	
697	scripts_dirs = []
698	
699	
700	def add_dir(path):
701	    if path and path not in scripts_dirs:
702	        scripts_dirs.append(path)
703	
704	
705	# next to the interpreter: where a virtualenv keeps its scripts.
706	# don't resolve symlinks here: a virtualenv's python is usually a link to the base
707	# interpreter, and following it would lead out of the environment we're inspecting.
708	add_dir(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(sys.executable)))
709	add_dir(sysconfig.get_path("scripts"))
710	try:
711	    # where `pip install --user` puts scripts
712	    add_dir(sysconfig.get_path("scripts", sysconfig.get_preferred_scheme("user")))
713	except Exception:
714	    add_dir(sysconfig.get_path("scripts", "nt_user" if os.name == "nt" else "posix_user"))
715	
716	candidates = record_candidates + [os.path.join(d, f) for d in scripts_dirs for f in filenames]
717	
718	path = None
719	for candidate in candidates:
720	    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
721	        path = candidate
722	        break
723	
724	print("__hcli__:" + json.dumps({
725	    "name": name,
726	    "path": path,
727	    "scripts_dirs": scripts_dirs,
728	    "record_candidates": record_candidates,
729	    "entry_point": entry_point,
730	}))
731	"""
732	
733	
734	# Script run by IDA's Python interpreter (not by idat).
735	# Invokes a console script by its entry point: import the module, call the attribute,
736	# exit with its return value. That is exactly what the wheel spec defines a console
737	# script to do, and what the generated wrapper contains, so this is behaviorally
738	# identical. Used when the wrapper itself can't be found on disk.
739	RUN_ENTRY_POINT_PY = r"""
740	import sys
741	from importlib.metadata import distributions
742	
743	name = sys.argv[1]
744	
745	for dist in distributions():
746	    try:
747	        eps = [
748	            ep

809	def get_environment_for_python(python_exe: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
810	    """Build the environment for a process run against the given Python.
811	
812	    hcli may itself run inside a virtualenv (or a uv cache overlay), so the
813	    inherited VIRTUAL_ENV/PYTHONHOME describe hcli's environment, not IDA's.
814	    """
815	    env = os.environ.copy()
816	
817	    env.pop("PYTHONHOME", None)
818	
819	    venv_root = _get_venv_root_from_python(str(python_exe))
820	    if venv_root:
821	        env["VIRTUAL_ENV"] = str(venv_root)
822	    else:
823	        env.pop("VIRTUAL_ENV", None)
824	
825	    scripts_dir = str(python_exe.parent)
826	    path = env.get("PATH")
827	    env["PATH"] = f"{scripts_dir}{os.pathsep}{path}" if path else scripts_dir

832	def _run_probe(python_exe: Path, src: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> dict:
833	    """Run a probe script with the given Python and parse its `__hcli__:` result line.
834	
835	    Raises:
836	        ProbeError: if the interpreter can't be run, fails, or emits no result.
837	    """
838	    argv = [str(python_exe), "-c", src, *args]
839	    logger.debug("probing IDA Python environment: %s", argv)
840	
841	    try:
842	        process = subprocess.run(
843	            argv,
844	            capture_output=True,
845	            text=True,
846	            encoding="utf-8",
847	            errors="replace",
848	            check=False,
849	            timeout=60.0,
850	            env=get_environment_for_python(python_exe),
851	        )
852	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
853	        raise ProbeError(f"failed to run {python_exe}: {e}") from e
854	
855	    if process.returncode != 0:
856	        raise ProbeError(f"{python_exe} exited with status {process.returncode}: {process.stderr.strip()}")
857	
858	    for line in process.stdout.splitlines():
859	        if line.startswith("__hcli__:"):
860	            return json.loads(line[len("__hcli__:") :])
861	
862	    raise ProbeError(f"no result from {python_exe}: {process.stdout.strip()}")

876	def render_script_not_found(info: ScriptInfo) -> str:
877	    """Explain why a console script couldn't be resolved to a path."""
878	    searched = "\n".join(f"  {d}" for d in info.scripts_dirs)
879	
880	    if info.entry_point:
881	        distribution = " ".join(filter(None, [info.entry_point.distribution or "?", info.entry_point.version]))
882	        return (

884	            f"but no program for it was installed.\n"
885	            f"Searched that distribution's file list and:\n{searched}\n"
886	            f"Try reinstalling {info.entry_point.distribution or distribution}."

895	    Returns the exit status of the command.
896	
897	    Raises:
898	        OSError: if the command can't be executed.
899	    """
900	    logger.debug("running: %s", list(argv))

902	    try:

911	def run_script(python_exe: Path, name: str, args: Sequence[str] = ()) -> int:
912	    """Run the console script `name` in the given Python environment.
913	
914	    Prefers the installed wrapper executable, so the script sees exactly what it
915	    would when invoked from the shell. Falls back to invoking the entry point
916	    directly when the wrapper isn't on disk, for example when an installer put it
917	    somewhere we don't know to look.
918	
919	    Returns the exit status of the script.
920	
921	    Raises:
922	        ProbeError: if the environment can't be inspected.
923	        ScriptNotFoundError: if no such script is installed.
924	    """
925	    info = get_script_info(python_exe, name)
926	
927	    if info.path is not None:
928	        if os.access(info.path, os.X_OK):
929	            return run_in_python_environment(python_exe, [str(info.path), *args])
930	        # a wrapper without the executable bit is still a Python script we can run.
931	        return run_in_python_environment(python_exe, [str(python_exe), str(info.path), *args])

933	    if info.entry_point is not None:

937	    raise ScriptNotFoundError(render_script_not_found(info))

35	def _get_uv_cache_dirs() -> list[Path]:
36	    """

38	    to store things like temporary virtual environments.
39	    """
40	    dirs: list[Path] = []

43	    if uv_cache:
44	        dirs.append(Path(uv_cache).resolve())
45	
46	    home = Path.home()

48	    if system == "Darwin":
49	        dirs.extend((home / "Library" / "Caches" / "uv", home / ".cache" / "uv"))
50	    elif system == "Windows":

66	    such as, "is the given virtual environment found in the cache directory?"
67	    """

86	def _has_uv_internal_parent(path: Path) -> bool:
87	    """Check if any ancestor directory has a UV-internal name.
88	
89	    UV organizes its cache into directories like ``archive-v0/`` and
90	    ``builds-v0/``.  These names are unique to UV's internal layout —
91	    no user would name their project directories this way.  This catches
92	    ephemeral environments regardless of where the cache root is
93	    (``~/.cache/uv/``, ``$TMPDIR``, ``--no-cache`` temp dirs, etc.).

98	def is_uv_cache_virtual_env(virtual_env: str | Path) -> bool:
99	    """Detect if a virtual environment is a UV ephemeral cache/overlay environment.
100	
101	    For example, if you run ``uv run --with ida-hcli hcli`` from a non-project
102	    directory, then uv may create a temporary virtual environment to run this
103	    command.  This routine detects if the given path is one of those cache
104	    environments.
105	
106	    Three independent signals (any is sufficient):
107	
108	      1. Path is under a known UV cache directory (``~/.cache/uv/``, etc.).
109	      2. Path has a UV-internal ancestor directory (``archive-v0/``,
110	         ``builds-v0/``).  Catches ``--no-cache`` and ``$TMPDIR`` layouts.
111	      3. pyvenv.cfg contains ``extends-environment`` — only written by
112	         ``uv run --with`` overlay environments (uv 0.7.9+).
113	    """
114	    path = Path(virtual_env)
115	
116	    if _is_under_uv_cache(path):
117	        return True
118	
119	    if _has_uv_internal_parent(path):
120	        return True

122	    cfg = parse_pyvenv_cfg(path / "pyvenv.cfg")
123	    return "extends-environment" in cfg

126	def get_python_exe_candidates(root: Path, version: str | None = None) -> list[Path]:
127	    """List the paths where a Python interpreter may live under an environment root.
128	
129	    The root can be a virtualenv or an installation prefix (sys.prefix); both
130	    use the same layout.  `version` is a `major.minor` string that adds the
131	    version-suffixed name (like `bin/python3.12`) to the candidates on POSIX.
132	    """
133	    if platform.system() == "Windows":
134	        return [root / "Scripts" / "python.exe", root / "python.exe"]

136	    bindir = root / "bin"

138	    if version:
139	        candidates.append(bindir / f"python{version}")
140	    candidates.extend([bindir / "python3", bindir / "python"])

148	    or when its interpreter is missing (such as a venv whose base Python was

158	def probe_python_version(python_exe: Path) -> str | None:
159	    """Probe the major.minor version of a Python interpreter by running it.
160	
161	    Returns None when the interpreter can't be run, so callers can treat this
162	    as best-effort.
163	    """
164	    try:
165	        result = subprocess.run(
166	            [str(python_exe), "-c", PRINT_VERSION_PY],
167	            capture_output=True,
168	            text=True,
169	            check=True,
170	            timeout=10.0,
171	        )
172	    except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError) as e:
173	        logger.debug("failed to probe version of %s: %s", python_exe, e)

180	def read_virtual_env_version(virtual_env: str | Path) -> str | None:
181	    """Read the `major.minor` Python version recorded in a venv's pyvenv.cfg.
182	
183	    The stdlib `venv` module writes `version`, while uv writes `version_info`;
184	    both are handled.  Returns None when pyvenv.cfg is missing or records no
185	    usable version.
186	
187	    This only reports what created the venv.  Prefer running the venv's
188	    interpreter when it's available, since a venv can be relocated or its base
189	    Python replaced after pyvenv.cfg was written.
190	    """
191	    cfg = parse_pyvenv_cfg(Path(virtual_env) / "pyvenv.cfg")
192	    raw = cfg.get("version") or cfg.get("version_info")
193	    if not raw:
194	        return None
195	
196	    parts = raw.split(".")
197	    if len(parts) < 2:
198	        return None
199	
200	    try:
201	        return f"{int(parts[0])}.{int(parts[1])}"
202	    except ValueError:
203	        return None

207	    """Detect the major.minor Python version of a virtual environment.
208	
209	    Runs the venv's own interpreter, which is authoritative, and falls back to
210	    the version recorded in pyvenv.cfg when the interpreter is missing or can't
211	    be run.  Returns None when neither is available.
212	    """
213	    python_exe = find_virtual_env_python(virtual_env)
214	    if python_exe is not None:
215	        version = probe_python_version(python_exe)
216	        if version:

219	    return read_virtual_env_version(virtual_env)

224	    path: Path
225	    source: str

228	def find_candidate_virtual_envs() -> list[VenvCandidate]:
229	    """Scan PATH for virtual environments that are not the current process venv.
230	
231	    When HCLI runs under `uv run --with ida-hcli`, uv replaces `$VIRTUAL_ENV`
232	     with its own ephemeral virtual environment.
233	    Based on our research, the user's real venv typically
234	     remains on `$PATH` (the `activate` script prepends its `bin/`).
235	
236	    This function recovers those candidates.
237	    """
238	    excluded: set[Path] = set()
239	    excluded.add(Path(sys.prefix).resolve())
240	
241	    seen: set[Path] = set()
242	    candidates: list[VenvCandidate] = []
243	
244	    path_val = os.environ.get("PATH", "")
245	    for entry in path_val.split(os.pathsep):
246	        if not entry:
247	            continue
248	
249	        entry_path = Path(entry)
250	        if entry_path.name not in ("bin", "Scripts"):
251	            continue
252	
253	        venv_root = entry_path.parent
254	        cfg_path = venv_root / "pyvenv.cfg"
255	        if not cfg_path.is_file():
256	            continue
257	
258	        try:
259	            resolved = venv_root.resolve()
260	        except OSError:
261	            continue
262	
263	        if resolved in excluded:
264	            continue
265	
266	        if resolved in seen:
267	            continue
268	        seen.add(resolved)
269	
270	        candidates.append(VenvCandidate(path=venv_root, source="PATH"))
271	
272	    return candidates

275	def resolve_user_virtual_env() -> Path | None:
276	    """Resolve the user's activated virtual environment.
277	
278	    If `$VIRTUAL_ENV` is set and is not a uv cache overlay, returns it
279	    directly.  If it *is* a uv cache overlay, scans `$PATH` for the
280	    first non-uv-cache candidate venv.  Returns None when no user venv
281	    can be identified.
282	
283	    When HCLI runs under `uv run --with ida-hcli`, uv replaces `$VIRTUAL_ENV`
284	     with its own ephemeral virtual environment.
285	    Based on our research, the user's real venv typically
286	     remains on `$PATH` (the `activate` script prepends its `bin/`).
287	    """
288	    virtual_env = os.environ.get("VIRTUAL_ENV")
289	    if not virtual_env:
290	        return None
291	
292	    if not is_uv_cache_virtual_env(virtual_env):
293	        hcli_prefix = os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(sys.prefix))
294	        if os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(virtual_env)) == hcli_prefix:
295	            return None
296	        return Path(virtual_env)
297	
298	    for candidate in find_candidate_virtual_envs():
299	        if not is_uv_cache_virtual_env(candidate.path):
300	            return candidate.path
301	
302	    return None

87	def install_plugin(
88	    ctx, plugin: str, editable: bool, config: tuple[str, ...], no_build_isolation: bool, upgrade: bool
89	) -> None:
90	    """Install a plugin from a repository, local directory, local .zip file, or URL."""
91	    pip_options: PipOptions = ctx.obj.get("pip_options", PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT)
92	    if no_build_isolation:
93	        pip_options = dataclasses.replace(pip_options, no_build_isolation=True)
94	    plugin_repo_obj = ctx.obj.get("plugin_repo")
95	    plugin_spec = plugin
96	    try:
97	        sweep_trash()
98	
99	        with rich.status.Status("collecting environment", console=stderr_console):
100	            current_ida_platform = find_current_ida_platform()
101	            current_ida_version = find_current_ida_version()
102	
103	        # Editable install: skip the archive pipeline entirely. Read metadata
104	        # straight from the source directory and symlink it into place.
105	        if editable:
106	            source_dir = Path(plugin_spec).expanduser()
107	            if not source_dir.exists():
108	                raise click.BadParameter(f"path does not exist: {plugin_spec}")
109	            if not source_dir.is_dir():
110	                raise click.BadParameter(
111	                    f"--editable requires a directory containing ida-plugin.json, got: {plugin_spec}"
112	                )
113	            source_dir = source_dir.resolve()
114	            try:
115	                metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_directory(source_dir)
116	            except ValueError as e:
117	                raise click.BadParameter(str(e))
118	            plugin_name = metadata.plugin.name
119	            buf = None  # sentinel: editable; no archive bytes
120	
121	        elif Path(plugin_spec).expanduser().is_dir() and (Path(plugin_spec).expanduser() / "ida-plugin.json").is_file():
122	            # Local non-editable install: pack the directory into an in-memory
123	            # zip and run it through the same archive pipeline used for zip /
124	            # URL / repo installs. The dir must contain ida-plugin.json -- any
125	            # bare directory name without metadata falls through so it can be
126	            # resolved as a repository plugin reference instead.
127	            logger.info("installing from the local file system (directory)")
128	            source_dir = Path(plugin_spec).expanduser().resolve()
129	            buf = pack_plugin_directory_to_zip(source_dir)
130	            items = list(get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive(buf))
131	            if len(items) != 1:
132	                raise ValueError("plugin directory must contain a single plugin")
133	            plugin_name = items[0][1].plugin.name
134	
135	        elif Path(plugin_spec).exists() and plugin_spec.endswith(".zip"):
136	            logger.info("installing from the local file system")
137	            buf = Path(plugin_spec).read_bytes()
138	            items = list(get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive(buf))
139	            if len(items) != 1:
140	                raise ValueError("plugin archive must contain a single plugin for local file system installation")
141	            plugin_name = items[0][1].plugin.name
142	
143	        elif plugin_spec.startswith("file://"):
144	            logger.info("installing from the local file system")
145	            # fetch from file system
146	            buf = fetch_plugin_archive(plugin_spec)
147	            items = list(get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive(buf))
148	            if len(items) != 1:
149	                raise ValueError("plugin archive must contain a single plugin for local file system installation")
150	            plugin_name = items[0][1].plugin.name
151	
152	        elif is_github_direct_install_url(plugin_spec):
153	            logger.info("installing from GitHub repository")
154	            try:
155	                owner, repo, tag = parse_github_url(plugin_spec)
156	                tag_info = f"@{tag}" if tag else " (latest release)"
157	                with rich.status.Status(
158	                    f"fetching plugin from GitHub: {owner}/{repo}{tag_info}", console=stderr_console
159	                ):
160	                    buf = fetch_github_release_zip_asset(owner, repo, tag)
161	            except (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException):
162	                console.print("[red]Cannot connect to GitHub - network unavailable.[/red]")
163	                console.print("Please check your internet connection.")
164	                raise click.Abort()
165	            items = list(get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive(buf))
166	            if len(items) != 1:
167	                raise ValueError("plugin archive must contain a single plugin for GitHub installation")
168	            plugin_name = items[0][1].plugin.name
169	
170	        elif plugin_spec.startswith("https://"):
171	            logger.info("installing from HTTP URL")
172	            try:
173	                with rich.status.Status("fetching plugin", console=stderr_console):
174	                    buf = fetch_plugin_archive(plugin_spec)
175	            except (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException):
176	                console.print(f"[red]Cannot connect to {plugin_spec} - network unavailable.[/red]")
177	                console.print("Please check your internet connection.")
178	                raise click.Abort()
179	            items = list(get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive(buf))
180	            if len(items) != 1:
181	                raise ValueError("plugin archive must contain a single plugin for HTTP URL installation")
182	            plugin_name = items[0][1].plugin.name
183	
184	        else:
185	            logger.info("finding plugin in repository")
186	            plugin_repo: BasePluginRepo = ctx.obj["plugin_repo"]
187	            try:
188	                ref = parse_plugin_reference(plugin_spec)
189	            except ValueError as e:
190	                raise click.BadParameter(f"invalid plugin reference: {plugin_spec!r}: {e}")
191	
192	            # reconstruct the plugin_spec for repo lookup without the @host suffix
193	            bare_spec = ref.name + ref.version_spec
194	            try:
195	                with rich.status.Status("fetching plugin", console=stderr_console):
196	                    plugin_name, buf = plugin_repo.fetch_compatible_plugin_from_spec(
197	                        bare_spec, current_ida_platform, current_ida_version, host=ref.host
198	                    )
199	            except AmbiguousPluginReferenceError as e:
200	                if ref.version_spec and not e.version_spec:
201	                    e = AmbiguousPluginReferenceError(e.name, e.candidates, ref.version_spec)
202	                console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: plugin name '{e.name}' is ambiguous")
203	                console.print("Choose one of:")
204	                for candidate_ref in e.candidate_refs:
205	                    console.print(f"  {format_qualified_plugin_reference(candidate_ref)}")
206	                raise click.Abort()
207	
208	        if not editable:
209	            assert buf is not None  # invariant: only the editable branch leaves buf as None
210	            _, metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_archive(buf, plugin_name)
211	        # else: `metadata` was already populated from the source directory.
212	
213	        # Same-name install conflict: another plugin with the same bare name is already
214	        # installed from a different repository. The install layout is
215	        # $IDAUSR/plugins/<name>, so only one same-name plugin can be installed at a time.
216	        # Use the archive metadata host (not the download URL) as the long-term identity
217	        # because GitHub redirects can cause the fetch URL and the metadata host to differ.
218	        try:
219	            installed = find_installed_plugin(plugin_name)
220	        except PluginNotInstalledError:
221	            installed = None
222	
223	        if installed is not None and normalize_plugin_host(installed.host) != normalize_plugin_host(
224	            metadata.plugin.host
225	        ):
226	            raise InstalledPluginNameConflictError(
227	                requested_name=plugin_name,
228	                requested_host=metadata.plugin.host,
229	                installed_name=installed.name,
230	                installed_host=installed.host,
231	                installed_path=installed.path,
232	            )
233	
234	        # `--upgrade` turns an already-installed plugin from an error into an
235	        # in-place upgrade, so callers that just want the plugin present (e.g.
236	        # `hcli mcp install`) can be run repeatedly. Editable installs already
237	        # replace whatever is at the destination, so there's nothing to do
238	        # there. Nothing newer to install is success, not an error.
239	        is_upgrade = False
240	        if upgrade and installed is not None and not editable:
241	            if parse_plugin_version(metadata.plugin.version) <= parse_plugin_version(installed.version):
242	                console.print(
243	                    f"[green]Already installed[/green] plugin: [blue]{plugin_name}[/blue]=={installed.version}"
244	                )
245	                return
246	            is_upgrade = True
247	
248	        if metadata.plugin.settings:
249	            for config_item in config:
250	                if "=" not in config_item:
251	                    raise ValueError(f"invalid config format: {config_item}, expected key=value")
252	                key, value_str = config_item.split("=", 1)
253	                descr = metadata.plugin.get_setting(key)
254	                parsed_value = parse_setting_value(descr, value_str)
255	                descr.validate_value(parsed_value)
256	
257	        if editable:
258	            install_plugin_directory_editable(source_dir, plugin_name, pip_options=pip_options)
259	        else:
260	            assert buf is not None
261	            if is_upgrade:
262	                write_archive = upgrade_plugin_archive
263	                status_text = "upgrading plugin"
264	            else:
265	                write_archive = install_plugin_archive
266	                status_text = "installing plugin"
267	            if isinstance(plugin_repo_obj, PluginBundleRepo) and not pip_options.has_custom_sources:
268	                current_python_version = detect_current_python_version()
269	                with bundle_dependency_source(
270	                    plugin_repo_obj, current_ida_platform, current_python_version
271	                ) as bundle_opts:
272	                    if bundle_opts is None:
273	                        available = ", ".join(plugin_repo_obj.target_ids) or "none"
274	                        console.print(
275	                            f"[red]Error[/red]: plugin bundle does not include dependencies"
276	                            f" for {current_ida_platform}, Python {current_python_version}."
277	                        )
278	                        console.print(f"Available targets in this bundle: {available}")
279	                        raise click.Abort()
280	                    effective_pip_options = merge_bundle_pip_options(pip_options, bundle_opts)
281	                    with rich.status.Status(status_text, console=stderr_console):
282	                        write_archive(buf, plugin_name, pip_options=effective_pip_options)
283	            else:
284	                with rich.status.Status(status_text, console=stderr_console):
285	                    write_archive(buf, plugin_name, pip_options=pip_options)
286	
287	        try:
288	            if metadata.plugin.settings:
289	                cli_config: dict[str, str | bool] = {}
290	                for config_item in config:
291	                    if "=" not in config_item:
292	                        raise ValueError(f"invalid config format: {config_item}, expected key=value")
293	                    key, value_str = config_item.split("=", 1)
294	                    descr = metadata.plugin.get_setting(key)
295	                    parsed_value = parse_setting_value(descr, value_str)
296	                    cli_config[key] = parsed_value
297	
298	                if cli_config:
299	                    for key, value in cli_config.items():
300	                        descr = metadata.plugin.get_setting(key)
301	                        descr.validate_value(value)
302	                        if descr.default != value:
303	                            set_plugin_setting(metadata.plugin.name, key, value)
304	                else:
305	                    needed_settings = [
306	                        s
307	                        for s in metadata.plugin.settings
308	                        if not has_plugin_setting(plugin_name, s.key) and s.required and s.default is None
309	                    ]
310	
311	                    if needed_settings and not console.is_interactive:
312	                        setting_names = ", ".join(f"--config {s.key}=<value>" for s in needed_settings)
313	                        raise ValueError(
314	                            f"plugin requires configuration but console is not interactive. Please provide settings via command line: {setting_names}"
315	                        )
316	
317	                    if console.is_interactive:
318	                        existing_config = get_ida_config()
319	                        existing_values: dict[str, str | bool] = {}
320	                        if plugin_name in existing_config.plugins:
321	                            existing_values = dict(existing_config.plugins[plugin_name].settings)
322	
323	                        answers = prompt_plugin_settings(metadata.plugin.settings, existing_values)
324	                        if answers is None:
325	                            raise click.Abort()
326	                    else:
327	                        answers = {}
328	
329	                    for key, answer in answers.items():
330	                        descr = metadata.plugin.get_setting(key)
331	                        if descr.default == answer:
332	                            continue
333	
334	                        set_plugin_setting(metadata.plugin.name, descr.key, answer)
335	
336	        except Exception:
337	            if is_upgrade:
338	                # The upgrade itself succeeded; the plugin the user already had
339	                # is now at the new version. Uninstalling it here would be a
340	                # worse outcome than leaving the settings unconfigured.
341	                logger.warning("failed to configure settings")
342	                raise
343	            logger.warning("failed to configure settings, removing installation...")
344	            with rich.status.Status("rolling back installation", console=stderr_console):
345	                uninstall_plugin(plugin_name)
346	            raise
347	
348	        suffix = " [yellow](editable)[/yellow]" if editable else ""
349	        verb = "Upgraded" if is_upgrade else "Installed"
350	        console.print(f"[green]{verb}[/green] plugin: [blue]{plugin_name}[/blue]=={metadata.plugin.version}{suffix}")
351	    except MissingCurrentInstallationDirectory:
352	        explain_missing_current_installation_directory(console)
353	        raise click.Abort()
354	
355	    except FailedToDetectIDAVersion:
356	        explain_failed_to_detect_ida_version(console)
357	        raise click.Abort()
358	
359	    except InstalledPluginNameConflictError as e:
360	        console.print(
361	            f"[red]Error[/red]: cannot install plugin "
362	            f"'{e.requested_name}@{e.requested_host}' because "
363	            f"'{e.installed_name}@{e.installed_host}' is already installed at {e.installed_path}"
364	        )
365	        console.print(f"Only one plugin with the bare name '{e.requested_name}' can be installed at a time.")
366	        console.print("Uninstall the existing plugin first, then install the other qualified plugin.")
367	        raise click.Abort()
368	
369	    except Exception as e:
370	        logger.debug("error: %s", e, exc_info=True)
371	        console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: {e}")
372	        raise click.Abort()

6	def _env_bool(name: str, default: bool = False) -> bool:
7	    """Parse a boolean environment variable using one consistent truthy set."""
8	    raw = os.getenv(name)
9	    if raw is None:
10	        return default
11	    return raw.strip().lower() in ("true", "yes", "on", "1")
12	
13	
14	def _env_optional(name: str) -> str | None:
15	    """An optional environment variable, treating set-but-empty as unset.
16	
17	    `export HCLI_IDAUSR=` leaves the variable set to "", which must not
18	    survive as an override: readers do `Path(ENV.HCLI_IDAUSR)`, and
19	    `Path("")` is the current directory.
20	    """
21	    return os.getenv(name) or None
22	
23	
24	def _env_int(name: str, default: int) -> int:
25	    """Parse an integer environment variable, falling back to *default* on a bad value.
26	
27	    Parsed at class-body eval and imported by the CLI entrypoint, so a malformed
28	    value must not raise — that would brick every command, not just the feature.
29	    """
30	    raw = os.getenv(name)
31	    if raw is None:
32	        return default
33	    try:
34	        return int(raw.strip())
35	    except ValueError:
36	        return default

121	def is_file_in_use_error(e: OSError) -> bool:
122	    """Does this error indicate a file locked by another process?
123	
124	    On Windows, deleting a DLL mapped by a running process fails with
125	    ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, and renaming any ancestor directory of an open file
126	    fails the same way. POSIX doesn't lock mapped files like this, but
127	    EBUSY/ETXTBSY can surface in similar situations.
128	    """
129	    if getattr(e, "winerror", None) in (5, 32):  # ACCESS_DENIED, SHARING_VIOLATION
130	        return True
131	    return e.errno in (errno.EACCES, errno.EPERM, errno.EBUSY, errno.ETXTBSY)

134	def move_plugin_directory_to_trash(path: Path, label: str = "") -> Path:
135	    """Atomically rename a plugin directory into the trash area.
136	
137	    Either the whole directory moves or nothing changes: when a file inside is
138	    locked (e.g. a plugin DLL loaded by a running IDA on Windows), the rename
139	    fails without modifying the installation.
140	
141	    The optional label is included in the trashed name (e.g. ".rollback") so
142	    a human inspecting the trash can tell what a leftover was.
143	
144	    Raises:
145	        PluginInUseError: when the rename fails because files are in use.
146	    """
147	    trash_dir = get_trash_directory(path.parent)
148	    trash_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
149	    destination = trash_dir / f"{path.name}{label}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
150	    try:
151	        os.rename(path, destination)
152	    except OSError as e:
153	        if is_file_in_use_error(e):
154	            raise PluginInUseError(path.name, path) from e
155	        raise
156	    return destination

159	def remove_plugin_directory(path: Path) -> None:
160	    """Remove a plugin directory transactionally.
161	
162	    First atomically rename the directory into the trash area, then delete the
163	    trashed copy. If deletion fails, the plugin is already logically removed;
164	    the leftover is swept by a later plugin command.
165	
166	    Raises:
167	        PluginInUseError: when files are in use; the installation is untouched.
168	    """

172	    except OSError as e:

176	def sweep_trash() -> None:
177	    """Best-effort cleanup of leftovers in the trash area.
178	
179	    Leftovers accumulate from interrupted operations: partially deleted
180	    uninstalls, staging directories, stale upgrade rollbacks. Call this only
181	    between plugin operations, never while one is in flight: an active upgrade
182	    keeps its rollback copy in the trash.
183	    """
184	    try:
185	        trash_dir = get_trash_directory()
186	        if not trash_dir.is_dir():
187	            return
188	        entries = list(trash_dir.iterdir())
189	    except Exception as e:
190	        logger.debug("could not enumerate trash directory: %s", e)
191	        return
192	
193	    for entry in entries:
194	        logger.debug("sweeping trash: %s", entry)
195	        try:
196	            if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
197	                shutil.rmtree(entry)
198	            else:
199	                entry.unlink()
200	        except OSError as e:
201	            logger.debug("could not sweep %s: %s", entry, e)

219	    """validate the `ida-plugin.json` metadata within the given plugin directory.
220	
221	    The following things must be checked:
222	    - the following paths must contain relative paths, no paths like ".." or similar escapes:
223	      - entry point
224	      - logo path

226	      - entry point
227	      - logo path

232	    if metadata.plugin.logo_path:

234

236

238	        # source plugin

240	            logger.debug(f"Entry point file not found in directory: '{metadata.plugin.entry_point}'")
241	            raise ValueError(f"Entry point file not found in directory: '{metadata.plugin.entry_point}'")
242	    else:
243	        # binary plugin - check for various extensions
244	        if not entry_point_path.exists():
245	            found = False
246	            for extension in (".so", ".dll", ".dylib"):
247	                if (plugin_path / (metadata.plugin.entry_point + extension)).exists():
248	                    found = True
249	                    break
250	            if not found:
251	                logger.debug(f"Entry point file not found in directory: '{metadata.plugin.entry_point}'")
252	                raise ValueError(f"Entry point file not found in directory: '{metadata.plugin.entry_point}'")
253	
254	    if metadata.plugin.logo_path:

256	        if not logo_path.exists():
257	            logger.debug(f"Logo file not found in directory: '{metadata.plugin.logo_path}'")

262	    """Does the path hold a well-formed installed plugin?
263	
264	    Mirrors the criteria of ``get_installed_plugin_records``: the manifest
265	    parses, referenced files exist, and the plugin name matches the directory
266	    name. A directory that fails this is debris, e.g. remnants of an
267	    interrupted uninstall (issue #228).

302	    """Enumerate installed plugins with their on-disk metadata.
303	
304	    This is the canonical source of truth for "what is installed". Other
305	    helpers (``get_installed_plugin_paths``, ``is_plugin_installed``, etc.)
306	    are implemented on top of this list so they agree on what counts as
307	    installed.
308	    """
309	    plugins_dir = get_plugins_directory()
310	    records: list[InstalledPluginRecord] = []
311	
312	    if not plugins_dir.exists():
313	        return records
314	
315	    for plugin_path in plugins_dir.iterdir():
316	        if not plugin_path.is_dir():
317	            continue

320	        if not metadata_file.exists():
321	            continue

454	def validate_can_install_python_dependencies(
455	    zip_data: bytes,
456	    metadata: IDAMetadataDescriptor,
457	    excluded_plugins: list[str] | None = None,
458	    python_exe: Path | None = None,
459	    pip_options: PipOptions = PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT,
460	) -> Path | None:
461	    """Verify Python dependencies can be installed.
462	
463	    Returns:
464	        The Python executable path if dependencies were validated, None if no dependencies needed.
465	
466	    Raises:
467	        PipNotAvailableError: If pip is not available in IDA's Python
468	        DependencyInstallationError: If dependencies cannot be installed
469	    """
470	    python_dependencies = get_python_dependencies_from_plugin_archive(zip_data, metadata)
471	    if python_dependencies:
472	        all_python_dependencies: list[str] = []
473	        for existing_plugin_path in get_installed_plugin_paths():
474	            existing_metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_directory(existing_plugin_path)
475	            if excluded_plugins and existing_metadata.plugin.name in excluded_plugins:
476	                continue
477	
478	            existing_deps = get_python_dependencies_from_plugin_directory(existing_plugin_path, existing_metadata)
479	            all_python_dependencies.extend(existing_deps)
480	
481	        all_python_dependencies.extend(python_dependencies)
482	
483	        if python_exe is None:
484	            resolved = resolve_current_python()
485	            python_exe = resolved.exe
486	            # These packages are about to be installed for a Python version that
487	            # IDA may not actually run, in which case IDA won't be able to import
488	            # them. Say so before spending time on the install.
489	            warn_on_python_version_mismatch(resolved.probe, python_exe)
490	            if is_externally_managed(resolved):
491	                raise DependencyInstallationError(
492	                    python_dependencies, externally_managed_environment_message(python_exe)
493	                )
494	        logger.debug(f"python: {python_exe}")
495	
496	        if not has_pip(python_exe):
497	            logger.debug("pip not available")
498	            raise PipNotAvailableError(python_exe)
499	
500	        try:
501	            verify_pip_can_install_packages(python_exe, all_python_dependencies, pip_options=pip_options)
502	        except CantInstallPackagesError as e:
503	            logger.debug("can't install dependencies: %s", e)
504	            raise DependencyInstallationError(python_dependencies, str(e)) from e
505	
506	        return python_exe
507	
508	    return None

511	def validate_can_install_plugin(
512	    zip_data: bytes,
513	    metadata: IDAMetadataDescriptor,
514	    current_platform: str,
515	    current_version: str,
516	    pip_options: PipOptions = PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT,
517	) -> Path | None:
518	    """Verify plugin can be installed.
519	
520	    Returns:
521	        The Python executable path if pip dependencies were validated, None otherwise.
522	
523	    Raises:
524	        InvalidPluginNameError: If plugin name is invalid
525	        PluginAlreadyInstalledError: If plugin is already installed
526	        BrokenPluginInstallationError: If remnants of a broken installation are in the way
527	        PlatformIncompatibleError: If current platform is not supported
528	        IDAVersionIncompatibleError: If current IDA version is not supported
529	        PipNotAvailableError: If pip is not available (when dependencies are needed)
530	        DependencyInstallationError: If dependencies cannot be installed
531	    """
532	    name = metadata.plugin.name
533	    try:
534	        destination_path = get_plugin_directory(name)
535	    except ValueError as e:
536	        logger.error(f"Can't install plugin: {e!s}")
537	        raise InvalidPluginNameError(name, str(e)) from e
538	
539	    # is_symlink() is checked in addition to exists() so a broken symlink
540	    # (dangling editable install) is reported rather than tripping up
541	    # extraction later.
542	    if destination_path.exists() or destination_path.is_symlink():
543	        if is_valid_plugin_directory(destination_path):

546	
547	        # The directory exists but doesn't hold a working plugin: remnants of
548	        # an interrupted install/uninstall (issue #228). Point the user at
549	        # uninstall, which knows how to remove broken directories, rather than
550	        # silently deleting data on the install path.
551	        logger.warning(f"Broken plugin directory: {destination_path}")
552	        raise BrokenPluginInstallationError(name, destination_path)

555	    if current_platform not in platforms:
556	        logger.warning(f"Current platform not supported: {current_platform}")
557	        raise PlatformIncompatibleError(current_platform, platforms)
558	
559	    if metadata.plugin.ida_versions and not is_ida_version_compatible(current_version, metadata.plugin.ida_versions):
560	        logger.warning(f"Current IDA version not supported: {current_version}")
561	        raise IDAVersionIncompatibleError(current_version, metadata.plugin.ida_versions)
562	
563	    return validate_can_install_python_dependencies(zip_data, metadata, pip_options=pip_options)

566	def validate_archive_entry(file_info: zipfile.ZipInfo, relative_path: pathlib.PurePosixPath) -> None:
567	    """Validate a ZIP archive entry before extraction.
568	
569	    This function prevents path traversal attacks by rejecting:
570	    - Symlinks (which can point outside the extraction directory)
571	    - Absolute paths
572	    - Paths containing '..' (parent directory references)
573	
574	    Raises:
575	        ValueError: If the entry is unsafe to extract
576	    """
577	    # Reject symlinks - they can escape the extraction directory
578	    # Unix symlink has file type 0xA in the high nibble of external_attr
579	    if (file_info.external_attr >> 28) == 0xA:
580	        logger.warning("Rejecting symlink in archive: %s", file_info.filename)
581	        raise ValueError(f"Symlinks not allowed in archive: {file_info.filename}")
582	
583	    # Reject absolute paths
584	    if relative_path.is_absolute():
585	        logger.warning("Rejecting absolute path in archive: %s", file_info.filename)
586	        raise ValueError(f"Absolute path in archive: {file_info.filename}")
587	
588	    # Reject path traversal sequences
589	    if ".." in relative_path.parts:
590	        logger.warning("Rejecting path traversal in archive: %s", file_info.filename)
591	        raise ValueError(f"Path traversal in archive: {file_info.filename}")

597	    Args:
598	      plugin_dir_prefix: the path within the ZIP archive to the plugin to extract
599	      file_info: the entry to consider
600	    """
601	    if not file_info.filename.startswith(plugin_dir_prefix):
602	        # only consider entries within the plugin directory
603	        return False
604	
605	    if file_info.filename == plugin_dir_prefix:
606	        # don't extract the plugin directory entry itself
607	        return False
608	
609	    if file_info.filename.startswith(plugin_dir_prefix + ".git/"):
610	        # don't extract git repo junk, which comes from manually archiving a plugin source repo
611	        return False
612	
613	    relative_path = pathlib.PurePosixPath(file_info.filename).relative_to(plugin_dir_prefix.rstrip("/"))
